claims.text: Date.parse loses time information - should use DateTime.parse or Time.parse to preserve full timestamp
Deprecated RSpec matcher be_true should be be true (with space)
Missing error handling for network and parsing failures in poll_feed method

The disqus.thor task now fetches each URL over HTTP via import_remote instead of parsing the offline XML export directly, and open(url) failures are not rescued, so pages that are offline or moved will break the whole batch import.

On line 35, `i.content` returns `nil` for RSS 2.0 feeds that use `<description>` instead of `<content>`, causing `NoMethodError` when `.scrub` is called on `nil`. Since the job has `sidekiq_options retry: false`, this crashes the entire feed polling job with no retry. Should fall back to `i.description` and guard against nil.
Destructive force: true in create_table migration will drop existing topic_embeds table and data
require_dependency is used on a gem (nokogiri) instead of a plain require; require_dependency is meant for autoloaded app code, not gems.
TopicEmbed.import mutates the caller's contents string argument in place via String#<<, an implicit side effect not indicated by the method's name or signature.

When `cook_method` is `:raw_html`, `cook` returns `raw` and bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. If any imported content isn't strictly sanitized upstream (RSS or remote fetch), this can become an XSS vector on Discourse-rendered pages.
i.content may be nil when RSS/Atom items have no content element, causing NoMethodError when calling .scrub on nil

Some feeds don't provide `content` for items; `i.content.scrub` will raise if `i.content` is `nil`, which would break polling. Need to guard/fallback to another field (e.g., description) before scrubbing/unescaping.
The new embed.css and embed.js assets are not added to config.assets.precompile, so in production the embed page and the third-party embed script will 404.
embed.js does not null-check the result of getElementById('discourse-comments') before appending to it, so a host page missing that container throws a TypeError that silently aborts the whole script.
embed.js silently requires discourseUrl to end with a trailing slash (undocumented), otherwise the constructed URL is malformed (e.g. http://forum.example.comembed/best).
XSS vulnerability: raw_html cook_method bypasses sanitizer, allowing untrusted HTML to become stored XSS
Assertions in after block is anti-pattern - if test body fails, after block still executes causing confusing errors
GET embed/best triggers creation of a Topic and Post as a side effect, violating the safety semantics of the GET method (RFC 9110), which can be triggered by prefetchers, link scanners, or retries.
retrieve_topic.rb has an unused require_dependency 'email/sender' that the file never references.
XSS vulnerability: request.referer is interpolated directly into a JavaScript string literal without any escaping, allowing an attacker to craft a Referer header to inject arbitrary JavaScript

force: true was added to an already-merged migration (and to a brand-new migration where it is unnecessary), which will silently DROP and recreate the table (destroying data) if the migration is ever rerun.
Destructive force: true in create_table migration will drop existing top_topics table and data
Four new files are missing a trailing newline at end of file.
Jobs::PollFeed#feed_key is defined but never called anywhere in the codebase, appearing to be unfinished dead code for a conditional-GET caching feature that isn't in this MR.
Port exclusion in absolutize_urls ignores scheme - an http:// URL on port 443 would have its port silently dropped, producing an incorrect absolute URL
An unrelated migration file (migrate_word_counts.rb) has a purely whitespace-only diff (trailing whitespace and trailing newline removed) that has nothing to do with the embedding feature.
Is it intentional that embed/best redirects to the login page on forums with login_required enabled, rather than supporting anonymous embedding?

TopicEmbed.import's check-then-create pattern doesn't handle the unique index conflict; concurrent imports of overlapping URLs can hit RecordNotUnique inside a transaction, rolling back the whole batch and aborting the polling loop.
postMessage height value should be parsed and validated before use to prevent invalid values

poll_feed's main body (the item-processing loop) is entirely mocked out via poller.expects(:poll_feed) in every test, so it has zero real test coverage and issues like missing sanitize or missing nil handling are invisible to CI.
Potential NoMethodError if feed item content is nil when calling .scrub
raw and cooked both set to p[:cooked] in disqus importer - raw should contain source text not HTML

Two poll_feed_spec tests never actually fail even if the guarded code they're supposed to test is deleted entirely, because they don't stub the other required guard conditions (feed_polling_enabled?), so they test the stub defaults rather than the code.
SSRF vulnerability using open(url) without validation

Is TopicRetriever synchronously running a full PollFeed cycle on every new embed request an intentional design choice, or an unintended amplification given it can trigger N full polling runs for N concurrent new URLs?
Only one of the three Gemfile lockfiles (Gemfile_rails4.lock) was updated with the new gems, so installs using the RAILS3 or RAILS_MASTER lockfiles will be out of sync with the Gemfile.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The disqus.thor rake task's --category option was removed when the import mechanism was switched, so any existing invocation that passes -c/--category will now fail as an unrecognized option.
Missing blank guard for SiteSetting.embed_by_username before calling downcase
import_remote missing timeout protection - open(url).read can hang indefinitely
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
Adding column with default + null: false in single migration step can cause long-running locks on large tables

RSS-imported HTML is stored via the raw_html cook method which completely bypasses PrettyText's sanitize step, and the output is rendered with raw, resulting in stored XSS; the import_remote path has a whitelist but the poll_feed path does not, so the two paths protect asymmetrically.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
Consider using image_tag for safer avatar rendering instead of direct URL interpolation
Missing guard against missing #discourse-comments container - appendChild will throw if the container doesn't exist
Non-atomic Redis setnx + expire pattern can leave key without TTL permanently blocking retrieval

Is the varchar(255) length of topic_embeds.embed_url sufficient for real-world URLs to be imported, given there's no length truncation and overly long URLs would abort the create inside a transaction?
content_sha1 updated unconditionally even if PostRevisor#revise! returns false, causing state desync
Unused feed_key method should be removed or connected to intended functionality
The disqus.thor task no longer passes created_at through to post creation, so all imported posts get the current time instead of their original Disqus timestamps, and this is irreversible.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
Sanitize `raw_html` posts before returning them - the early return turns imported embed HTML into stored, unsanitized output
cook_method option not validated before persisting, risking invalid enum values
